newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Elf Nigeria begins work on gas project.
newsitem.headline: Elf Nigeria begins work on gas project.

text.p: Elf Petroleum Nigeria Ltd said Tuesday it had begun work on its Obite gas project in the Delta region designed to supply 23.5 percent of the gas for Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas (NLNG) when it begins production in 1999.

An Elf spokesman told the News agency of Nigeria that the Obite gas project, designed to produce 7.15 million cubic metres of gas daily, would in addition produce 18,000 barrels of oil and condensates per day.
Elf holds a 15 percent stake in the NLNG venture in which Shell Gas BV, Agip SpA and state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) are also stakeholders.
Condensate, an extra light crude not counted in the oil output of OPEC, is at present produced in Nigeria only by the Mobil/NNPC joint venture.
The Obite project, the spokesman said, would include the laying of 140 kilometres of 20-inch pipes from Obite to Bonny, site of the NLNG plant on the Atlantic coast.
The primary objective of the Elf gas venture was to meet the company's quota of gas supply to the LNG plant for its estimated life-span of 22 years, he added.
